_: TIME RUNS ON THE BEAT — and this one is confirmed by eye, not by a compile. A clock's RATE is a lane read from the clip's own audio, so time itself accelerates: on a hit the sweep races and a whole coherent chunk of a later moment lands intact, then it slows and smears. ONSETS, not envelope: an envelope gives a gentle wobble, onsets give visible JOLTS, which is what running on a beat should look like. Both the head and the write follow `pulse`, so the whole transport pulses rather than one half of it drifting against the other. WANTS A CLIP WITH AUDIO and a legible picture — a mostly-black source makes the rhythm impossible to read. Proof it is live rather than compiling-and-doing-nothing: over a 10s run the pulse clock reaches ~13.5s while master reaches 10.0s. That number can only differ if the rate varied.
